properties.natural_language: Before receipt generation, the transaction must have completed execution (either success or revert) — the status code must be set to exactly 1 (success) or 0 (failure), with no other values permitted.
After ACTION-SET-STATUS-ONE completes, the receipt status field must equal exactly 1 (0x01), indicating successful execution.
After ACTION-SET-STATUS-ZERO completes, the receipt status field must equal exactly 0 (0x00), indicating failed execution.

The receipt status code must be bijectively determined by the execution outcome: success maps to 1, any revert/exception maps to 0. A block producer must not set status=1 for a reverted transaction or status=0 for a successful transaction.
After ACTION-STORE-RECEIPT, the receipt must be included in the block's receipt trie and be retrievable by transaction index. The receipt must be immutable once stored.
For blocks at or above BYZANTIUM_FORK_BLKNUM, receipts must use the new format with status code. For blocks below, receipts must use the old format with intermediate state root.

When an RPC client queries a transaction receipt, the receipt status code must accurately reflect the original execution outcome. The node must not reinterpret or modify the status code during retrieval.
The receipt status code value space is exactly {0, 1}. Any receipt containing a status code outside this set is malformed and must be rejected during block validation.
Before get_safe_beacon_block_root is called, the fork choice store must contain a justified_checkpoint with a non-zero root that references a block present in the block store.
After get_safe_beacon_block_root returns, the returned root must equal store.justified_checkpoint.root exactly.

After get_safe_execution_block_hash, if the block epoch >= BELLATRIX_FORK_EPOCH, the returned hash must be the execution payload block_hash from the beacon block. If epoch < BELLATRIX_FORK_EPOCH, the returned value must be Hash32() (empty).

The safe block must always be a descendant of (or equal to) the finalized block. The justified checkpoint root used as safe block must reference a block on the canonical chain as seen by an honest supermajority.

The safe block hash communicated to the EL via Engine API (forkchoiceUpdated safeBlockHash) must be derived from the justified checkpoint. The EL must treat this as advisory and not assume it is finalized.
A type-2 transaction submitted via JSON-RPC must have max_fee_per_gas >= current block base_fee_per_gas. Transactions with insufficient max fee must be rejected before mempool admission.
Before mempool acceptance, the sender must have balance >= (gas_limit * max_fee_per_gas) + value. This ensures worst-case gas cost coverage.
The transaction must follow EIP-2718 type-2 format with all required fields (max_fee_per_gas, max_priority_fee_per_gas, access_list). Missing or malformed fields must cause rejection.
After effective gas price computation, the priority fee paid to the validator must equal min(max_priority_fee_per_gas, max_fee_per_gas - base_fee_per_gas) * gas_used.

The base fee must be deterministically computable from the parent block header alone. Given parent_base_fee, parent_gas_used, and parent_gas_target, the new base fee is uniquely determined with no randomness or external input.

When parent gas_used == gas_target, the base fee must remain unchanged. When gas_used > target, base fee must increase by at least 1. When gas_used < target, base fee must decrease (but never below 0).
The maximum base fee increase per block is 12.5% (1/8). The base fee can never increase by more than parent_base_fee / BASE_FEE_MAX_CHANGE_DENOMINATOR in a single block.

A received block must have gas_limit within ±1/1024 of parent gas_limit, gas_limit >= 5000, gas_used <= gas_limit, and base_fee_per_gas matching the deterministic calculation from parent. Violation of any rule must cause block rejection.

For every executed transaction: total_sender_debit = gas_used * effective_gas_price + value. Of the gas payment, base_fee * gas_used is burned, priority_fee * gas_used goes to validator, and (gas_limit - gas_used) * effective_gas_price is refunded to sender. No ETH is created.
After base fee burn, the burned amount (gas_used * base_fee_per_gas) must be permanently removed from the total supply. No account balance may increase by this amount.
After constructing a Deneb light client header for a block at epoch >= DENEB_FORK_EPOCH, the header must include blob_gas_used and excess_blob_gas fields populated from the execution payload.

Before building a light client header, the block must be finalized and the execution payload must be available. The blob_gas_used and excess_blob_gas fields must be extracted from the actual execution payload, not from any external source.

Light client headers for blocks before DENEB_FORK_EPOCH must NOT include blob_gas_used or excess_blob_gas fields. Headers for blocks at or after DENEB_FORK_EPOCH must include them. This boundary must be enforced consistently across all full nodes.
Light client requests via P2P must be rate-limited. Deneb-format headers must only be served for blocks at or after DENEB_FORK_EPOCH. Pre-Deneb blocks must use the legacy header format.

The compute_fork_version function must evaluate fork epochs in descending order (EIP6800 first, then DENEB, CAPELLA, etc.). If the current epoch >= EIP6800_FORK_EPOCH, the EIP-6800 fork version must be returned.

After fork digest derivation, the resulting ForkDigest must be the first 4 bytes of hash_tree_root(ForkData(fork_version, genesis_validators_root)). This digest must be used in all gossip topic names.

When a peer connection is requested, the remote peer's advertised fork digest must be verified against the local node's expected fork digest for the current epoch. Peers with mismatched fork digests must be disconnected.
At any given epoch, there is exactly one valid fork version and one valid fork digest. All honest nodes must agree on the fork version for a given epoch.
The Fulu fork transition must only occur at an epoch boundary (slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH == 0) and only when compute_epoch_at_slot(slot) == FULU_FORK_EPOCH (411392).
After upgrade_to_fulu, fork.previous_version must equal the Electra fork version, fork.current_version must equal FULU_FORK_VERSION (0x06000000), and fork.epoch must equal the current epoch.
After proposer lookahead initialization, the proposer_lookahead array must contain exactly (MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1) * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH entries, each containing a valid validator index.

During the Fulu fork transition, all Electra state fields (validators, balances, slashings, participation flags, sync committees, pending consolidations, pending deposits, pending partial withdrawals) must be preserved byte-for-byte. Only fork metadata and proposer_lookahead are modified.

The fork transition must be validated: epoch boundary alignment must be confirmed, and after the upgrade, state field preservation must be verified. Failure in either check must reject the fork transition.
The proposer lookahead computation must be deterministic: given the same beacon state at the fork boundary, all nodes must produce identical proposer_lookahead arrays.
Before computing excess blob gas, the blob schedule must be loaded and the parent header must be available with valid excess_blob_gas and blob_gas_used fields.

The blob base fee computation must use the blob_schedule.baseFeeUpdateFraction from the currently active fork entry. The excess blob gas target must be GAS_PER_BLOB * blob_schedule.target (not the deprecated TARGET_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK constant).

The EL blob schedule and CL blob schedule must be consistent: EL max must equal CL MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK * GAS_PER_BLOB, and EL activation timestamps must align with CL epoch boundaries. Misalignment is a configuration error.

After a BPO fork activates, the new blob parameters (target, max, baseFeeUpdateFraction) must be used immediately for the next block's excess blob gas and base fee calculations. No transition period or interpolation is used.

At a BPO fork boundary, the fork digest must rotate. The ENR nfd field must be updated to advertise the next upcoming fork. Gossip topics must use the new ForkDigestValue. Peers on the old fork digest must be disconnected.

For EIP-155 transaction signing, the signing data must be RLP-encoded with exactly nine elements: (nonce, gasprice, startgas, to, value, data, CHAIN_ID, 0, 0). The CHAIN_ID must match the target network.
After signing, the v parameter must equal {0,1} + CHAIN_ID * 2 + 35, where {0,1} is the y-value parity of the ECDSA signature. This encodes the chain ID for later extraction.

When validating a received signed transaction, the v parameter format must be checked: v=27 or v=28 indicates legacy format (6-element hash recovery), v>28 indicates EIP-155 format (9-element hash recovery with chain ID extraction). Invalid v values must cause transaction rejection.
For EIP-155 format transactions, the chain ID extracted via (v - 35) / 2 must match the network's CHAIN_ID. Transactions with mismatched chain IDs must be rejected.

An EIP-155 signed transaction valid on chain A (CHAIN_ID=X) must always be invalid on chain B (CHAIN_ID=Y, X≠Y). The chain ID embedded in v creates a cryptographic binding between the transaction and its target chain.
Legacy transactions (v=27/28) lack cross-chain replay protection and may be valid on multiple chains. This is an accepted backward-compatibility risk.
CHAIN_ID must be a positive integer (> 0). CHAIN_ID=0 must be treated as invalid, as it would produce v=35/36 which conflicts with valid EIP-155 chain IDs.
After successful signature validation (whether legacy or EIP-155), the recovered public key must yield a valid Ethereum address that becomes the transaction sender.

When eth_sendTransactionToContractFunction is called, the ABI-derived function selector (first 4 bytes of keccak256 of function signature) must match the first 4 bytes of the transaction data field. Mismatch must cause the wallet to reject or warn.

A matching 4-byte function selector does NOT guarantee the ABI accurately describes the contract's behavior. Function selector collisions are possible (different function signatures can produce the same 4-byte selector). The wallet must communicate this limitation to the user.
The ABI JSON must be well-formed and parseable. Malformed ABI JSON must be rejected before any validation or display occurs.

After ABI validation passes and display is rendered, the user must be shown the function name and decoded parameters. The displayed information must clearly indicate that the ABI source is an untrusted DApp.
The selector comparison must be performed as a strict 4-byte equality check: keccak256(function_signature)[0:4] == transaction_data[0:4]. No fuzzy matching or partial comparison is acceptable.
The user must explicitly approve or reject the transaction after reviewing displayed information. No automatic approval based on ABI validation is permitted.

The bloom filter is a 256-byte (2048-bit) array. Each entry sets exactly 3 bits derived from the first 6 bytes of keccak256(entry), using the least significant 11 bits of 16-bit words at byte indices (0,1), (2,3), (4,5).
Bloom filter bits are monotonically set (OR-only). Once a bit is set to 1, it must never be cleared back to 0 during the construction of a single receipt's bloom filter. The filter is append-only.

After logs_bloom completes, the resulting 256-byte Bloom must contain bits set for every log address and every log topic from all logs in the transaction. Missing any entry is a correctness violation.

A bloom filter match (all query bits present) does not guarantee the log exists — false positives are inherent. A bloom filter non-match (any query bit missing) guarantees the log does NOT exist in that block — no false negatives are possible.

Log queries via RPC (eth_getLogs) must first perform bloom filter pre-filtering, then verify actual log matches for blocks that pass the bloom check. Bloom-only results must not be returned to clients.

Transactions submitted via JSON-RPC (eth_sendRawTransaction) from untrusted users must undergo full validation: EIP-1559 fee field checks, EIP-155 chain ID verification, signature recovery, nonce check, and balance check before mempool admission.
Transactions received via P2P gossip (devp2p) require identical validation to RPC-submitted transactions. Additionally, EIP-155 chain ID check must be performed to reject cross-chain replay attempts.

Blocks received via P2P gossip must be validated: EIP-1559 base fee must match deterministic calculation from parent, gas limit within ±1/1024 of parent, gas_used <= gas_limit, minimum gas limit >= 5000, and all receipt status codes must correctly reflect execution outcomes.

DApp-provided ABI metadata via eth_sendTransactionToContractFunction must be treated as untrusted. The wallet must validate the function selector match and clearly indicate the ABI source is external.
RPC query parameters for receipt/log queries must be validated. Rate limiting should be applied to prevent resource exhaustion from bloom filter lookups on large block ranges.

The CL-to-EL Engine API channel must be JWT-authenticated. The EL must independently validate all payload content from the CL, including block structure and state transitions. The safe block hash must be treated as advisory, not finalized.

CL P2P peer connections must verify fork digest compatibility. During fork transitions (Fulu, EIP-6800, EIP-7892 BPO forks), peers with mismatched fork digests must be disconnected. The ENR nfd field must be validated.
The bloom filter must be initialized as a 256-byte zero-filled array before any entries are added. Using an uninitialized or pre-populated array would produce incorrect filter results.
The gas target is always exactly 50% of the gas limit (gas_target = gas_limit / ELASTICITY_MULTIPLIER where ELASTICITY_MULTIPLIER = 2). Blocks can use up to 2x the target gas.
For the first EIP-1559 block (London fork), the base fee must be set to INITIAL_BASE_FEE (1 Gwei). All subsequent blocks must compute base fee from parent.
For genesis networks starting at Fulu, fork.previous_version should be set to FULU_FORK_VERSION (same as current_version) since there is no prior fork.

The blob schedule must define entries in chronological order. At any given block/epoch, exactly one blob schedule entry is active. The active entry is determined by the most recent activation timestamp (EL) or epoch (CL) that has passed.

All revert conditions (REVERT opcode, out-of-gas, invalid opcode, stack underflow/overflow, and any EVM exception) must map to status code 0. Only a fully successful top-level call produces status code 1.

The beacon block store must contain the block referenced by the justified checkpoint root. If the block is missing, the safe head computation must fail gracefully rather than returning a stale or incorrect hash.
